review:
Blast space pirates out of the sky like an 80s arcade game except... you're actually in the game in a 3D world. You get a shield, weapon options, power ups, different game modes, and more. 

Banger music, guns go pew pew, and space pirates that you need to save the universe from. What more could you want?

Tip - If you have a Rift S or similar headset you will likely want to go into Steam settings and disable haptics for this game. Due to the Rift S design, your headset tracking has to compete for the same USB bandwidth which can cause the tracking issues/frame stutters that other people are mentioning in comments.

My overall review of Space Pirate Trainer VR…
Space Pirate Trainer remains one of the most effective pure arcades in VR: tight, physical, and endlessly replayable for score hunters, but limited if you’re after long campaigns, narrative depth, or couch‑friendly play.

__No Tutorial – This was a big issue for me. Other then more possible graphics changes in the settings, not having a proper tutorial I think is a big miss. I started the game spending a while just to figure out who to change different ammo types, how to get the shield, different shield types, etc… Would have been nice just to have a quick one-minute tutorial.
__Graphics – I wish there were more settings options for this game. Most of the graphics feel that they are not as polished or varied as big-budget VR action games, which I thought this could be on par for but some of the textures (especially the flying ball) just look almost too dull.
__ Relatively Simple Formula — Can get repetitive, core mechanics (wave shooting, endurance) can feel repetitive compared with deeper VR shooters or narrative titles.
__Room-Scale — I would same for some of the game play you could play on a mat, but for most and maybe even in all, I’d really recommend a larger playing area, (maybe 8’ x 8’). I know for some people having this large of a play Arena are impractical for many users.
__Limited long-form content — while highly replayable, it lacks a substantial single-player campaign or varied mission structure that some players want. I wish there was some more level progression or expansion as you play. Like maybe you unlock more weapon options as you play? Just an idea.

I bought this game over eight years ago. I was going through my VR library to see what games I had played, and what I hadn't. Saw this game only had about 30 mins of play. Figured I'd give it another go, as I remembered it positively from the early days of VR.

The game seems to have changed a bit, IIRC. Seems to be a bit more fleshed out. It's definitely fun. Cool weapons, defensive options, and power ups. There are four different modes to play. I went through one round of each, just to see what they are. They are pretty much the same, some easier, some much harder.

The graphics in the game are pretty good for how old the game is, pretty good in general actually. Probably better than some modern games. Though it's all robots, space, and lasers, so hard to screw up.

The game is definitely worth playing for a bit. I can only spend so much time in a wave shooter if there isn't a bit more to it, so I only played for another 30 minutes or so. It's a great way to introduce someone to VR though, as there is no locomotion, and you could even play seated, since as far as I could tell, you don't have to look behind you. Though, I guess in an office chair you could spin if that were the case. But, a good party game or introduction for new people. Didn't interest me enough to play it much more than that.

Full price is a bit much for me, given what I got out of it. Half price is fair for me. Got 1.1 hours out of it, it's fun, and now it'll sit in my library to one day be a potential demo for someone.
